items.t: Said she has concerns about putting $12.5M of taxpayer dollars into the account created under House Bill 4071 with no sure oversight or accountability.
items.q: “I have many concerns about putting $12.5M of our taxpayer dollars into an account with no sure oversight or accountability,” said Leader Munson.

items.t: Said a historic budget is one that funds public education, protects Medicaid enrollment and uses extra dollars for tax relief for working Oklahomans, in a statement on SB 1177.
items.q: What makes a budget historic is funding public education that gets us out of last in the nation, ensuring not a single person is cut from Medicaid when the federal government fails us, and using every extra dollar we have to provide real tax relief for working Oklahomans.

items.t: Said the Governor's executive order on verifying documentation status for program applicants threatens the public health and safety of children in Oklahoma.
items.q: “The Governor’s executive order threatens the public health and safety of children in Oklahoma,” said House Democratic Leader Cyndi Munson, D-Oklahoma City.

items.t: Supports directing more money to public schools, including a competitive pay increase for teachers and support staff (2025).
items.q: Imagine that amount of money going to our public schools to lower class sizes, increase counselors and school nurses, and provide a competitive teacher and support staff pay increase.

items.t: Was against the expansion of the Parental Choice Tax Credit in HB 3705, which was signed into law.
items.q: released the following statement condemning the expansion of the Parental Choice Tax Credit, HB 3705, signed into law.

record.t: Filed HR 1059 with Rep. Andy Fugate and Rep. Daniel Pae to recognize May 2026 as Asian American Pacific Islander Month.
record.q: House members Leader Cyndi Munson, D-Oklahoma City, Rep. Andy Fugate, D-Del City, and Rep. Daniel Pae, R-Lawton, filed HR 1059 to recognize May 2026 as Asian American Pacific Islander Month.

record.t: Was re-elected House Democratic Leader for the 60th Legislature in May 2023.
record.q: In May of 2023, she was re-elected as House Democratic Leader for the 60th Legislature.

record.t: Was elected House Democratic Leader for the 59th Legislature by her Democratic colleagues in May 2021.
record.q: In May of 2021, she was elected by her Democratic colleagues as the House Democratic Leader for the 59th Legislature.

record.t: Was selected to take part in the Council of State Governments Henry Toll Fellowship Program in 2019.
record.q: In 2019, she was selected to participate in the Council of State Governments Henry Toll Fellowship Program, one of the nation’s premiere leadership development programs for state government officials.

record.t: Was elected to the Oklahoma Legislature in September 2015, the first Asian-American woman elected to it.
record.q: Elected in September of 2015, Cyndi became the first Asian-American woman elected to the Oklahoma Legislature.

record.t: Was appointed to the Board of Directors of the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee for a three-year term.
record.q: Cyndi was recently appointed to the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee – the official party committee dedicated to electing Democrats to statehouses – Board of Directors, where she will serve a three-year term.

record.t: Debated against House Bill 4071 on the House floor; the bill advanced.
record.q: Oklahoma House Democratic Leader Cyndi Munson, D-Oklahoma City, debated against House Bill 4071 which advanced off the House floor today.
